title: Qm Bell Models And Measurement Limits

items.title: Binary correlation models: setting-indexed tables of two-valued outcome laws, marginals and the CHSH functional
items.statement:
This item fixes finite combinatorial vocabulary for outcome laws of a
two-station comparison. No physical interpretation, measurement model,
dynamics or locality assertion is made here; the physical readings are fixed
on the page of this pair. No choice principle is used.

**(a) Binary correlation model.** Let $I$ and $J$ be finite nonempty sets, the
**setting labels** of the two stations, and put
$\Sigma:=\{-1,+1\}$ for the common **outcome labels**. A **binary correlation
model** on $(I,J)$ is a family
$$\mu=(\mu_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J},\qquad \mu_{ij}:\Sigma\times\Sigma\to[0,1],$$
of functions with the normalization
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=1 \qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in I\times J$$
([[def-finite-sum]]). Each $\mu_{ij}$ is the **joint law** of the setting pair
$(i,j)$: it is the outcome-weight function of a finite probability space on
the four outcomes $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ in the sense of
[[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]], and sums over $\Sigma\times\Sigma$
are finite sums.

**(b) Marginals.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$ the **marginal law of the first
station** and the **marginal law of the second station** are
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon):=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma .$$

**(c) No-signalling.** The model $\mu$ is **no-signalling** when the marginal
law of the first station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}$ for all $i\in I$ and all $j,j'\in J$, and the
marginal law of the second station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $j\in J$ and all $i,i'\in I$. The word is
used as a name for this pair of identities about the tables; no spatial or
causal claim is attached to it.

**(d) Correlations and the CHSH functional.** Assume $I=J=\{0,1\}$. The
**correlation** of the setting pair $(i,j)$ and the **CHSH functional** of the
model are the real numbers
$$E_{ij}(\mu):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma} \varepsilon\,\delta\,\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad S(\mu):=E_{00}(\mu)+E_{01}(\mu)+E_{10}(\mu)-E_{11}(\mu).$$

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) introduce finite tables, their marginals, the
no-signalling identities and one linear functional of four correlations. They
assert no physical assumption, no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law
for a real apparatus and no statement about nature; the identification of a
laboratory arrangement with a model $\mu$ is a separate physical matter.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section II.A, PDF pages 2-3: the two-station measurement scenario, the joint table p(ab|xy), its marginals and the independence of a marginal from the distant setting

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the four pairwise outcome laws of a two-station spin comparison and the expectation values built from them

items.title: Local-response representations of a binary correlation model: one setting-independent specification space and per-station response laws
items.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]). No choice principle is used in
this definition.

**(a) Local-response representation.** A **local-response representation** of
$\mu$ is a tuple consisting of a probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},
\mathbb P)$ ([[def-measure-space]], [[def-probability-measure]]) and two
families of **response laws**
$$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I},\qquad (\beta_{j})_{j\in J},$$
where for each $i\in I$ the function
$\alpha_{i}:\Lambda\times\Sigma\to[0,1]$ has the two properties
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=1\quad(\lambda\in\Lambda), \qquad \lambda\mapsto\alpha_{i}(\lambda,+1)\ \text{is measurable}$$
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]), and the family
$(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ has the same two properties; and the **representation
identity**
$$\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\, d\mathbb P(\lambda) =\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\!\left[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\, \beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\right]$$
holds for every $(i,j)\in I\times J$ and every
$(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$. The integrand is a product of two
bounded measurable $[0,1]$-valued functions, so the expectation exists as a
finite number ([[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]],
[[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). The functions
$\alpha_{i}(\cdot,-1)=1-\alpha_{i}(\cdot,+1)$ and likewise for $\beta_{j}$ are
measurable as well. The variable $\lambda$ is called the **specification**
of the representation; it is a mathematical index, and no physical
interpretation is asserted.

**(b) Response functions (deterministic form).** Equip the finite outcome set
$\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ with its discrete $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal P(\Sigma)$.
A local-response representation **has response functions** when there are
measurable maps
$a_{i}:(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})\to(\Sigma,\mathcal P(\Sigma))$ $(i\in I)$
and $b_{j}:(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})\to(\Sigma,\mathcal P(\Sigma))$
$(j\in J)$ with
$$\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=\mathbf 1_{\{a_{i}=\varepsilon\}}(\lambda), \qquad \beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)=\mathbf 1_{\{b_{j}=\delta\}}(\lambda),$$
in which case the representation identity reads
$$\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\mathbb P\bigl(\{a_{i}=\varepsilon\}\cap\{b_{j}=\delta\}\bigr).$$
The deterministic form is a special case of clause (a): it is obtained by
setting the response laws to the Dirac laws at $a_{i}(\lambda)$ and
$b_{j}(\lambda)$. In this form one and the same specification space and the
same single-station functions $a_{i}$ and $b_{j}$ serve every setting
pair, and the response of a station depends on the specification and on that
station's own setting only.

**(c) Terminology.** The two mathematical features named by **local response**
are: (i) a single specification space carrying the probability law used for
every setting pair (setting-independence), and (ii) per-station response laws
that do not depend on the distant station's setting. A model that admits such
a representation is also called a **local model** of the tables in the
literature; the representation is an existence statement about the tables and
asserts no determinism, no mechanism, no dynamics and no causal relation. In
particular clause (a) permits probabilistic responses and does not require
the response functions of clause (b).

**(d) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) fix vocabulary. They assert no physical
assumption and no property of any laboratory arrangement; whether a declared
physical model of a comparison admits a representation of this form is a
mathematical question about its tables, and the physical reading of that
question is fixed on the page of this pair.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF page 3: the local decomposition p(ab|xy) = integral of q(lambda) p(a|x,lambda) p(b|y,lambda), its factorability reading and the assumption that the settings are chosen independently of lambda

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 113-115 (PDF pages 121-123): response functions of the two stations on a common hidden-variable space and the expectation values they define

items.title: Local-response representability implies setting-independent marginals
items.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]), and suppose that $\mu$ admits a
local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})$, $(\beta_{j})$
and probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then:

(a) for every $i\in I$ the marginal law of the first station satisfies
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}\qquad\text{for all }j,j'\in J,$$
and for every $j\in J$ the marginal law of the second station satisfies
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $i,i'\in I$; that is, $\mu$ is
no-signalling;

(b) consequently, if a binary correlation model is not no-signalling, then it
admits no local-response representation.

No physical assumption and no choice principle is used; the proposition is a
statement about the tables and their representation.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF page 3: a marginal p(a|x) = sum over b of p(ab|xy) is independent of the distant setting y, and this is identified with the no-signalling property of the local decomposition

items.title: The CHSH bound for every binary correlation model admitting a local-response representation
items.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the setting sets $I=J=\{0,1\}$
with outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$, with correlations $E_{ij}(\mu)$ and
CHSH functional $S(\mu)$ as in
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clauses (d), and suppose that
$\mu$ admits a local-response representation with response laws
$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$, $(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then
$$\bigl|S(\mu)\bigr|\le 2 .$$
The statement is a theorem about the tables and their representation; it
asserts no measurement, no dynamics, no spatial or causal structure, and it
contains no physics. No choice principle is used.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF page 3, equation (4) and its derivation: the CHSH inequality S <= 2 for probabilities satisfying the local decomposition with local expectations in [-1,1]

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 113-115 (PDF pages 121-123): Bell's inequality for a setting-independent response-function model, obtained by bounding the response product pointwise

items.title: Conditioning on a setting-independent selection preserves local-response representability and the CHSH bound
items.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]), and suppose that $\mu$ admits a
local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$,
$(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Let
$D\in\Sigma_{\Lambda}$ be a **selection event** with $\mathbb P(D)>0$, put
$$\mathbb P_{D}(A):=\frac{\mathbb P(A\cap D)}{\mathbb P(D)}\qquad(A\in\Sigma_{\Lambda})$$
for the **conditional probability measure** on $D$, and define the
**$D$-conditional tables**
$$\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\frac{1}{\mathbb P(D)} \int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{D}(\lambda)\,\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\, \beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\,d\mathbb P(\lambda)$$
for $(i,j)\in I\times J$ and $(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$. Then:

(a) $\mathbb P_{D}$ is a probability measure on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})$
and $\mu^{D}:=(\mu^{D}_{ij})$ is a binary correlation model on $(I,J)$;

(b) the same response laws represent $\mu^{D}$ over $\mathbb P_{D}$:
$$\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\, d\mathbb P_{D}(\lambda)\qquad\text{for all }i,j,\varepsilon,\delta ;$$

(c) if $I=J=\{0,1\}$, then $\bigl|S(\mu^{D})\bigr|\le2$.

The selection event $D$ is a subset of the specification space: membership in
$D$ is the same for every setting pair and does not depend on the settings or
on the outcomes. No choice principle is used.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF page 3: the decomposition p(ab|xy) = integral of q(lambda) p(a|x,lambda) p(b|y,lambda), in which the settings are chosen independently of the specification lambda; conditioning on a specification-only event reweights q

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 113-115 (PDF pages 121-123): experimental tests of Bell's inequality and the qualification that a recorded sample is a sub-ensemble of the pairs produced

items.title: Singlet pairings: the joint laws of the two spin-half factors along two directions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis
of the tensor construction cited below. Let $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the
orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and let
$$\sigma_{x}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{y}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{z}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
be the Pauli matrices of clause (e) of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] in the ordered basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$; for $a=(a_{x},a_{y},a_{z})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$\sigma_{a}:=a_{x}\sigma_{x}+a_{y}\sigma_{y}+a_{z}\sigma_{z}$, and for
$\varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ put
$$P_{a,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,\sigma_{a}\bigr).$$
Let $V\widehat\otimes V$ be the completed tensor product with inclusion
$\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and let
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr)\in V\widehat\otimes V, \qquad q:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) for every unit $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$ the
operator $P_{a,\varepsilon}$ is an orthogonal projection on $V$,
$P_{a,+}+P_{a,-}=I$ and
$P_{a,\varepsilon}P_{a,\varepsilon'}=\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}P_{a,\varepsilon}$;

(b) $\|\Psi\|=1$ and the four vectors $\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),
\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})$ are mutually orthogonal, so
$(\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-}))$ is an
orthonormal basis of $V\widehat\otimes V$;

(c) for all unit $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and all
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a\cdot b\bigr);$$

(d) the marginals of the four numbers in (c) are
$$\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12 =\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle,$$
and their correlation is
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\,\delta\, \bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =-a\cdot b .$$

The lemma is a finite-dimensional computation in the tensor product; it
asserts no preparation, measurement or physical interpretation. The Axiom of
Countable Choice enters only through the construction of the completed tensor
product cited from [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 7.5.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 181-183): the spin-half Pauli matrices and the two-particle singlet as a difference of product basis vectors, and Section 6.1.4 printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the singlet spin correlations along two directions

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Sections 3 and 5, chapter pages 9-12 and 16-19: the Bell basis, the singlet state and its spin correlations; Chapter 2 'Spin One-Half' for the Pauli matrices

items.title: Declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework: two spin-half factors, four directions, joint sign tables and local-response models
items.statement:
## Definition

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3, the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5 as inherited through the cited
spin-$s$ model and spin-spectrum result (only their internal-factor content
is used here), the
internal-factor assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6 and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), together with the
composite, observable and measurement readings of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared spin-half factors.** A **declared spin-half factor** is the
internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ of the spin-$s$ model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with spin label
$s=\tfrac12$, with its orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, the self-adjoint
matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) and the spin
observables $S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, read as assigned sharp observables with unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and P6
clause (ii). For a unit direction $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clause (c) the
observable $S_{n}$ has the two eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$ with
spectral projections
$$P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,n\cdot\sigma\bigr), \qquad \varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\},$$
and the label $\varepsilon$ attached to the projection $P_{n,\varepsilon}$ is
the **sign label** of the outcome; the outcome coordinate is
$\varepsilon\hbar/2$, read in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, while the sign label
itself is dimensionless.

**(b) Declared arrangement.** A **declared spin correlation arrangement**
consists of: the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared
spin-half factors, with inclusion $\kappa$, in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] (a
declared pair of distinguishable subsystems whose assigned spaces are the two
internal factors); a **declared preparation** $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$,
the set of density operators on the composite
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); and two unit
**setting directions** $a_{0},a_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the first station and
$b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the second station. The setting labels are
$I=J=\{0,1\}$.

**(c) Declared local sign measurements.** For the first station and setting
$i\in I$, the **declared local sign measurement** is the declared ideal sharp
measurement whose outcome structure is the pair
$(P_{a_{i},+}\otimes I,\;P_{a_{i},-}\otimes I)$ with the sign labels $\pm1$:
these are the spectral projections of the local readout of the assigned
observable $(S_{a_{i}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ on the declared composite, the local
readout being constructed through the spectral measure by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] and
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]]. The second station's
declared local sign measurement for setting $j$ is
$(I\otimes P_{b_{j},+},\;I\otimes P_{b_{j},-})$, defined symmetrically.

**(d) Declared joint sign measurement and tables.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$
the **declared joint sign measurement** of the setting pair is the declared
ideal sharp measurement of the composite whose outcome structure is
$$E_{ij}:=\bigl(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}\bigr)_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma}, \qquad E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta},$$
with the pair of sign labels as its labels: by clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] each factor is an
orthogonal projection, and the tensor calculus of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] gives
$E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)E_{ij}(\varepsilon',\delta')=
\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}\delta_{\delta\delta'}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$
and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=I$, so this is a
finite family of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, as
required by clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Its
**outcome law** in the declared preparation $\rho$ is
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr), \qquad (\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma,$$
read from clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
(compare P2 clause (ii), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).
The **correlation table of the arrangement** is the family
$\nu^{\rho}=(\nu^{\rho}_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, which is a binary
correlation model on $(I,J)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a); its correlations
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$, its marginals and its CHSH functional $S(\nu^{\rho})$ are
the ones of clauses (b) and (d) of that definition, and are written
$S(\rho;a_{0},a_{1};b_{0},b_{1})$ when the arrangement data are displayed.

**(e) Declared local-response models of the arrangement.** A **declared
local-response model of the arrangement** is a local-response representation,
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]], of the
correlation table $\nu^{\rho}$. It is a model of the same four tables: it
consists of a probability space of **specifications** and of per-station
response laws, subject to the representation identity, and it need not be a
model of the framework's state space. The arrangement **admits a
local-response model** when such a representation exists.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix model vocabulary. They assign no spatial
position, worldline, spatial separation or temporal order to the two factors;
they assert no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus, no detection procedure
and no measured correlation; they do not assert that the composite is prepared
by any particular laboratory procedure. Whether a laboratory arrangement
realizes the declared preparation, the declared directions and the declared
sign measurements is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this
definition; the model's assignments of states to preparations and of spectral
projections to quantities are the readings of P1, P2 and P3 fixed on the
earlier pages.

## Remarks

- **Why the joint measurement is declared and not derived.** The framework's
  measurement vocabulary declares outcome structures; it does not assert that
  arbitrary observables of two factors possess a joint sharp measurement. For
  the arrangement the product family of clause (d) is itself a finite family
  of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, so the joint
  measurement of the two sign measurements is a declared ideal sharp
  measurement of the composite in the framework's own sense. No claim is made
  that an arbitrary pair of laboratory procedures realizes it.
- **Sign labels versus coordinates.** The sign labels $\pm1$ are the outcome
  indices used by the correlation tables; the physical outcome coordinates are
  $\pm\hbar/2$ in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. The correlation and the CHSH
  functional of clause (d) are functionals of the sign labels and are
  dimensionless; no numerical value of an angular momentum coordinate is
  asserted anywhere.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Section 5, chapter pages 16-19: the two-observer spin comparison, its four measurement choices and the joint probabilities p(ab|xy)

N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF pages 2-3: the two-station scenario with two measurement choices per station and its joint table

items.physical_scope: The declared model vocabulary of a two-station spin comparison inside the framework: two declared spin-half internal factors, a declared composite preparation, two declared unit directions per station, the four declared joint sign measurements with their outcome laws, the correlation table and the CHSH functional, and the class of local-response models of that table. The definition adds no physical assumption beyond P1, P2, P3, P5, P6 and P7 in their stated readings; P5 is inherited through the massive spin-s model and the spin-spectrum supplier, with only their internal-factor content used here. It assigns no spatial position, worldline, separation or temporal order to the factors, asserts no dynamics, no apparatus realization, no measured correlation and no empirical fact, and leaves the identification of a laboratory arrangement with these declarations to the tested identification of P7.

items.title: The singlet arrangement: directional sign tables, CHSH value 2 sqrt 2 and the failure of local-response models at violating settings
items.statement:
Adopt the declared spin correlation arrangement of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: the composite
$V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared spin-half factors with orthonormal basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$, a declared preparation $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, the
setting directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and the four
declared joint sign measurements with outcome laws
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\bigr), \qquad P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\,a\cdot\sigma) .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of
the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), and
take the **singlet preparation**
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr), \qquad \rho_{\Psi}:=T_{\Psi,\Psi},$$
where $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is the rank-one operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Then:

(a) for every $(i,j)\in\{0,1\}^{2}$ and all $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\bigl\langle(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a_{i}\cdot b_{j}\bigr);$$

(b) the correlations of the arrangement are
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$ and
$$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}) =-\bigl[a_{0}\cdot b_{0}+a_{0}\cdot b_{1}+a_{1}\cdot b_{0}-a_{1}\cdot b_{1}\bigr] =-\,(a_{0}\cdot(b_{0}+b_{1})+a_{1}\cdot(b_{0}-b_{1}));$$
in particular, for the unit directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ and
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2>2$;

(c) consequently the correlation table $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}$ of the arrangement
at those directions admits no local-response model in the sense of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: there is no local-response
representation of the four tables
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]) with these laws;

(d) the marginal sign laws of the arrangement are
$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac12=
\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},B}_{ij}(\delta)$ for every setting pair and every direction, so
the table is no-signalling in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]; and a discarded declared local
instrument on either factor leaves the reduced preparation of the other factor
and every local outcome law of that factor unchanged
([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).

The item is a conditional model computation: it asserts no measured
correlation, no apparatus and no empirical fact, and its exclusion is exactly
of the declared local-response class of these four tables. Higher singleton
claims about hidden variables in general are not asserted.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Section 5, chapter pages 16-19: the singlet state, the probabilities P(a,b), the EPR-type definite-spin ensemble and the Bell inequality P(a,b) <= P(a,c) + P(c,b) that it violates

N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section II.C.1.a, PDF pages 12-13: the Bell operator of the CHSH expression and the quantum bound 2 sqrt 2, attained by the singlet correlations

items.physical_scope: A conditional model computation for the declared spin correlation arrangement in the singlet preparation of two declared spin-half factors: the four directional sign tables, their correlations, the CHSH value at the specified directions, the setting-independent marginals and the failure of local-response representability at settings whose CHSH value exceeds 2. The item is a thought experiment of the declared framework; it asserts no spatial separation, no temporal order, no relativistic consideration, no apparatus, no detection and no measured correlation, and it excludes only the declared class of local-response models of these tables, not hidden-variable theories in general.

items.title: Tsirelson bound for every declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework
items.statement:
Let $(V\widehat\otimes V,\rho,a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1})$ be a declared spin
correlation arrangement of the two declared spin-half factors in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], with a preparation
$\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, unit directions
$a_{i},b_{j}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, outcome laws
$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and CHSH functional
$S(\nu^{\rho})$ as in clauses (d) of that definition and (d) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the hypotheses of the cited mathematical
suppliers. Then:

(a) $\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho})\bigr|\le2\sqrt2$ for every preparation $\rho$ and all
unit directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}$;

(b) the bound is attained: with $\Psi:=\frac1{\sqrt2}(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+}))$
and the singlet preparation $\rho_{\Psi}=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$, for the directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$,
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has
$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2$.

The statement is a conditional theorem about the declared arrangement model; it
asserts no measured value and no apparatus realization.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section II.C.1.a, PDF pages 12-13: the Bell operator of a Bell expression, the CHSH operator, the identity S^2 = 4 + [A1,A2][B1,B2], the conclusion ||S|| <= 2 sqrt 2 and the attainment by the singlet

L. J. Landau, 'On the violation of Bell's inequality in quantum theory', Physics Letters A 120 (1987) 54-56, as reported in the review above: the operator derivation of the CHSH quantum bound used here is verified directly from the operator identity in the proof

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the singlet correlation -a.b and the contrast with the bound of a setting-independent response model

items.physical_scope: A conditional bound on the CHSH functional of every declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework: for any declared composite preparation of the two spin-half factors and any two unit directions per station the absolute value of the CHSH functional of the arrangement's sign tables is at most 2 sqrt 2, and the bound is attained by the singlet preparation at the directions displayed on this page. The statement is a model theorem under the framework's composite, observable, measurement and spin readings; it asserts no measured value, no apparatus, no detection efficiency and no empirical fact.

items.title: Measurement-model boundaries of the singlet-local comparison: what the no-go excludes and what it does not
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the comparison establishes.** For the declared spin correlation
  arrangement of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], the four sign
  tables are the laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ of clause (d) of
  that definition. If the arrangement's CHSH functional satisfies
  $|S(\nu^{\rho})|>2$, then the four tables admit no local-response model:
  every local-response representation would give $|S|\le2$ by
  [[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]. The singlet at the
  directions of [[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] is the
  displayed instance, with $|S|=2\sqrt2$. The statement is a conditional
  no-go for one precisely defined class of models of one precisely defined set
  of four tables.

- **What is not excluded.** The theorem concerns models of the four tables
  that consist of one specification space whose probability law is the same
  for all setting pairs, together with per-station response laws that do not
  depend on the distant setting ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]
  clauses (a), (c)). Models outside that class are not addressed: a model
  whose specification or response is allowed to depend on the distant setting,
  a model that does not reproduce all four tables simultaneously, or a model
  of a different arrangement or of a different measurement structure is not
  excluded. In particular the comparison does not rule out "hidden variables"
  in general, and it does not claim that no completion of quantum mechanics
  exists; it excludes the declared local-response class for these tables.

- **Assumptions used.** The deduction rests on the framework readings P1, P2,
  P3, P5, P6 and P7 fixed by
  [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], on the declared composite,
  preparation and spin-half assignments, on the ideal sharp character of the
  declared measurements ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
  on the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom
  of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) stated in the arrangement and
  singlet-attainment hypotheses, and on the cited mathematics (the
  finite-dimensional tensor calculus, the CHSH bound for representable models
  and the operator bound of
  [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). Changing one of these
  readings voids the conditional conclusion for the changed model; it does not
  weaken it, and a replacement conclusion needs its own proof.

- **Measurement-model boundary.** The declared sign measurements have exactly
  two outcomes with sign labels $\pm1$; detection efficiency, finite
  resolution, dark counts, background, drift and loss are outside the
  arrangement and require their own apparatus models. In particular an
  observed violation on a recorded sub-ensemble does not by itself contradict
  the declared model class: the recorded tables are conditional tables, and
  the CHSH bound transfers to them when the selection is determined by a
  positive-probability event of the specification space that is the same for
  every setting pair, as in
  [[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]; that lemma is a
  sufficient condition, not a necessary one, and is not a claim about any
  real detector. A different selection model may also yield representable
  conditional tables; its consequences require their own justification. Finite
  samples add a sampling model and its fluctuations, treated on the examples
  page. Whether a finite record deductively excludes one of two specified
  models depends on their sampling supports: a record with positive
  probability under both is compatible with both, while an observed
  zero-probability record can exclude one specified ideal model conditional on
  its assumptions. No universal claim is made about every model pair or every
  finite sample.

- **No-signalling is not the separator.** Every local-response model is
  no-signalling ([[prop-nrqm-bell-local-representations-are-no-signalling]]),
  and every declared arrangement's marginals are also setting-independent:
  summing its joint law over $\delta$ gives
  $\nu^{\rho,A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_i,\varepsilon}\otimes I))$
  because $\sum_\delta P_{b_j,\delta}=I$, and the symmetric sum is
  $\nu^{\rho,B}_{ij}(\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I\otimes P_{b_j,\delta}))$
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clauses (a), (d)). For the
  singlet both marginals are $1/2$
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] clause (d)); a discarded
  declared local instrument on one factor leaves the other factor unchanged
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).
  The contrast between the two classes therefore lies in the joint tables,
  not in any dependence of one station's marginal law on the distant setting.

- **Attainment and sharpness.** The value $2\sqrt2$ is attained for the
  declared arrangement
  ([[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]] clause (b)), so within
  the declared class of binary sharp readouts of self-adjoint involutions no
  smaller uniform bound for the CHSH functional is available. This says
  nothing about other functionals, other numbers of settings, unsharp
  measurements or other systems.

- **Interpretation.** The result is a statement about four probability
  tables. It identifies no mechanism, no influence between the stations and
  no preferred frame; the arrangement carries no spatial or temporal
  structure. Interpretations that attach additional physical content to the
  violation are not part of the deduction and are not asserted here. Whether
  a laboratory arrangement realizes the declared model and what a recorded
  sample shows are separate matters under the preparation and apparatus
  postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A and Section II.C.1.a, PDF pages 2-3 and 12-13: the definition of a local model, the CHSH inequality and the quantum bound, and the distinction between the declared model class and broader interpretations

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the setting-independent response-function model, the Bell inequality it satisfies and the qualifications of the experimental discussion

items.physical_scope: A record of the boundaries of the comparison between the declared spin correlation arrangement and the declared class of local-response models: the exact class excluded, the assumptions on which the conditional exclusion rests, the ideal sharp character of the declared measurements, the separate detection, selection and finite-sample models needed for any comparison with recorded data, and the no-signalling properties shared by both sides. Setting-independent specification selection is a sufficient condition for transfer of the CHSH bound, not a necessary condition. The remark asserts no empirical result and no claim about nature.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the Bell-models page: conditional model results and the deferred experiment destination
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Mathematical vocabulary for binary correlation
  models and their local-response representations
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]],
  [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]), the CHSH bound for every
  representable model ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]),
  the preservation of representability and of the bound under a
  setting-independent selection
  ([[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]), the exact joint
  laws of the two-factor singlet ([[lem-nrqm-bell-singlet-pairings]]), the
  declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]), the singlet computation with
  the failure of local-response representability at violating settings
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]]) and the Tsirelson bound
  with its attainment
  ([[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). All are conditional
  model statements; the spin-arrangement and spin-comparison claims carry the
  Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Choice
  ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) stated in their supplier hypotheses.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment item, no reported count,
  no calibration, no detector efficiency, no loss model, no background, no
  trial-level uncertainty analysis, no p-value, no confidence level and no
  measured correlation. None of the computations establishes that the
  framework or any of its postulates describes nature, and none of them
  asserts that any laboratory procedure realizes the declared arrangement.
  The marginals, tables and correlations are model probabilities for the
  declared preparation; the identification of a concrete apparatus with the
  declared measurements is the
  tested identification with uncertainty of clause (iii) of the preparation
  and apparatus postulate P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Treating repetitions
  as independent and identically distributed draws is the additional
  statistical model of clause (ii), to be declared and checked for the
  apparatus and procedure; it is not implied by the state postulate.

- **Deferred experiment destination.** The design of this pair reserves an
  experiment item for a Bell test. Such an item is not built here: it would
  require reading a primary or authoritative full report and recording its
  source-specific preparation and apparatus, calibration, measured outputs,
  trial count where reported, detection efficiency, loss and post-selection,
  background, the reported statistical treatment and systematics, and the
  source's omissions; none of the sources read for this page supplies that
  level of detail. The sources' experimental remarks motivate the model
  comparison only: Binney's section 6.1.4 refers to the 1972
  Freedman-Clauser test and cites a 1998 photonic test, and the MIT chapter
  closes with the statement that experiments have confirmed violations; no
  numerical value from those secondary accounts is reproduced here as an
  observation, and no interval, count or precision is asserted. The
  statistics and primary-report gap named in the design is recorded as an
  open destination.

- **Source qualifications not imported.** The same sources contain general
  conclusions that the comparison rules out hidden variables as such or that
  quantum mechanics cannot be superseded by a theory with a definite spin
  direction. Those conclusions are stronger than the conditional statement
  proved here — which excludes only the declared local-response class of the
  declared tables — and are not imported. Likewise the operator bound used on
  this page is proved by the operator-norm route of the cited mathematics
  (the identity for the square of the CHSH operator and the norm bound,
  invoked in [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]] fact F6 and
  proof step 1.2). That route uses
  $\|[A_0,A_1]\|\le2$ and $\|[B_0,B_1]\|\le2$ for the supplier's
  self-adjoint involutions $A_i,B_j$, where $[A,B]:=AB-BA$ is the
  commutator; no
  reversed variance inequality of the form
  $\langle C^{2}\rangle\le\langle C\rangle^{2}$ is
  used as a premise.

- **What a comparison with data could show.** Under declared preparation,
  detection, settings, selection and sampling models, agreement of recorded
  frequencies with the arrangement's tables supports the combined model and
  apparatus assumptions. The bound $|S(\mu)|\le2$ constrains the correlations
  of a local-response model's probability tables, rather than every finite
  sample estimate $\widehat S$. A finite recorded estimate with
  $|\widehat S|>2$ can have positive probability under that model; finite-sample
  fluctuations are treated in [[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]]. Evidence
  against a specified model class requires an explicit statistical test with
  its sampling assumptions, uncertainty and error control, together with the
  apparatus and selection qualifications. A threshold crossing alone does
  not deductively exclude the class, and a p-value is not the probability
  that the class is false. Agreement does not prove the framework, and a null
  or reduced result does not by itself falsify it.

- **Interpretation and scope of the model.** The arrangement assigns no
  spatial positions, separation or temporal order to the two factors, so no
  relativistic locality principle is modelled here; the exclusion is a
  statement about the four tables. The boundaries of the comparison are
  recorded in [[rem-nrqm-bell-boundaries-and-comparison-scope]], and no
  interpretation of the violation beyond those boundaries is asserted.

references.title: N. Brunner et al., Bell nonlocality, Section VII.B.3, PDF page 52: finite statistics and conditional statistical evidence against local models

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the EPR/Bell discussion, the mention of the 1972 test and the citation of a 1998 photonic test, together with its unsupported general conclusions, which this page does not import

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Section 5, chapter pages 16-20: the singlet, the definite-spin ensemble, the Bell inequality, and the closing statement that experiments show the inequalities violated, without trial-level detail

items.physical_scope: A scope and evidence record for the page: the conditional model items it contains, the empirical content it does not contain, the qualifications of the sources' experimental remarks that are not imported, and the deferred destination of a Bell-test experiment item with its required preparation, apparatus, calibration, loss and statistical qualifications. The record distinguishes apparatus identification under P7(iii) from additional repeated-trial sampling assumptions under P7(ii), and asserts no empirical result, no measured correlation and no claim about nature.

title: Qm Bell Models And Measurement Limits — Examples

items.title: Worked Bell angles: the singlet against the EPR product mixture at the same directions
items.statement:
Adopt the declared spin correlation arrangement of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] over the two declared spin-half
factors $V,V$ with basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice, as required
by the cited singlet, spin-spectrum and arrangement suppliers
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix the orthonormal vectors
$e_{1}:=(1,0,0)$, $e_{2}:=(0,1,0)$, $e_{3}:=(0,0,1)$ and the four unit
directions
$$a_{0}:=e_{3},\qquad a_{1}:=e_{1},\qquad b_{0}:=\frac{e_{3}+e_{1}}{\sqrt2},\qquad b_{1}:=\frac{e_{3}-e_{1}}{\sqrt2}.$$
Consider two arrangements over these same directions:

- the **singlet arrangement**, with the singlet preparation
  $\rho_{\Psi}=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$,
  $\Psi=\frac1{\sqrt2}(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+}))$;
- the **product-mixture arrangement**, with the EPR-type mixture
  $$M:=\tfrac12\,T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},\,e_{+}\otimes e_{-}} +\tfrac12\,T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},\,e_{-}\otimes e_{+}} ,$$
  a convex combination of the two product preparations of definite opposite
  spins along $e_{3}$.

Then:

(a) for the singlet arrangement the four correlations are
$$E_{00}=E_{01}=E_{10}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\qquad E_{11}=+\frac{1}{\sqrt2}, \qquad S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2 ;$$

(b) for the product-mixture arrangement the four sign tables are
$$\nu^{M}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\, (a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}\bigr),$$
so its correlations are $E_{ij}=- (a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}$; at the displayed
directions $(a_{0})_{3}=1$, $(a_{1})_{3}=0$ and
$(b_{0})_{3}=(b_{1})_{3}=1/\sqrt2$, hence
$$E_{00}=E_{01}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\qquad E_{10}=E_{11}=0,\qquad S(\nu^{M})=-\sqrt2 ;$$

(c) the mixture's tables admit a local-response model
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]): on the two-point
specification space, the response laws
$$\alpha_{i}(1,\varepsilon)=\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3}),\quad \alpha_{i}(2,\varepsilon)=\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3}),\quad \beta_{j}(1,\delta)=\tfrac12(1-\delta(b_{j})_{3}),\quad \beta_{j}(2,\delta)=\tfrac12(1+\delta(b_{j})_{3})$$
with specification weights $\tfrac12,\tfrac12$ reproduce
$\nu^{M}$; consequently $\bigl|S(\nu^{M})\bigr|=\sqrt2\le2$, as the bound for
representable models requires
([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]);

(d) both arrangements have the same marginal sign laws
$\nu^{A}(\pm)=\nu^{B}(\pm)=\tfrac12$ for every direction, and the same reduced
preparation $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\tfrac12I=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho_{\Psi}$
on each factor, although their joint tables and CHSH functionals differ:
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2>2\ge\sqrt2=\bigl|S(\nu^{M})\bigr|$.

All clauses are conditional computations in the declared framework; no
measured correlation is asserted.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Section 5, chapter pages 16-19: the singlet probabilities P(a,b) at orthogonal and 45-degree directions and the EPR-type ensemble of definite opposite spins, with P(z,-z)=1/2 and P(z,x)=1/4

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the singlet correlation -a.b, the four-case expectation of the product, and the EPR discussion of an ensemble with definite opposite spins

items.physical_scope: A finite conditional computation in the declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework at four specified directions: the singlet's four sign tables and CHSH value, the tables and CHSH value of the EPR-type product mixture of definite opposite spins, an explicit local-response representation of the mixture's tables, and the comparison of the two arrangements. The example asserts no measured correlation, no apparatus and no empirical fact; it makes no claim that any laboratory preparation realizes either arrangement.

items.title: Finite samples of a declared arrangement: the CHSH estimator, its concentration and the limits of a finite-sample verdict
items.statement:
Adopt a declared spin correlation arrangement $(V\widehat\otimes V,\rho,
a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1})$ of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]
with its outcome laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$, correlations
$E_{ij}=E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$ and CHSH functional
$S=S(\nu^{\rho})$. Let $n\ge1$ and declare the following **sampling model**
(the statistical model of clause (ii) of the preparation and apparatus
postulate P7, [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): on a
probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ let
$$\bigl(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk}\bigr)_{\substack{i,j\in\{0,1\}\\ k\in\{1,\dots,n\}}}$$
be $4n$ random elements with values in $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ that are
**mutually independent** and have the declared laws
$$\mathbb P\bigl((\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})=(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr) =\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) \qquad\text{for every }i,j,k,\varepsilon,\delta$$
([[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]],
[[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). Define the **sample
correlations** and the **sample CHSH functional**
$$\widehat E_{ij}:=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{n}\Sigma_{ijk}\mathrm T_{ijk}, \qquad \widehat S:=\widehat E_{00}+\widehat E_{01}+\widehat E_{10}-\widehat E_{11}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathbb E[\widehat E_{ij}]=E_{ij}$ and
$\operatorname{Var}(\widehat E_{ij})\le1/n$ for all $(i,j)$;

(b) $\mathbb E[\widehat S]=S$, $\operatorname{Var}(\widehat S)\le4/n$, and
for every $\varepsilon>0$
$$\mathbb P\bigl(|\widehat S-S|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{4}{n\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$

(c) threshold consequences: if the declared model satisfies
$S\le2-\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, then
$\mathbb P(\widehat S>2)\le4/(n\varepsilon^{2})$; if the declared model is
the singlet arrangement with $S=-2\sqrt2$ and
$\varepsilon:=2\sqrt2-2$, then
$\mathbb P(\widehat S\ge-2)\le4/(n\varepsilon^{2})$. Moreover, for every
declared acceptance criterion $C\subseteq(\Sigma\times\Sigma)^{4n}$ that
rejects at least one outcome sequence $(x_{ijk})$ with
$\prod_{i,j,k}\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(x_{ijk})>0$, the failure probability of the
criterion is at least $\prod_{i,j,k}\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(x_{ijk})>0$;

(d) scope: the independence, the identical distribution and the tables
$\nu^{\rho}$ are declared model assumptions of the sampling model, not
consequences of P1-P6; clauses (a)-(c) assert no measured count, no p-value,
no error rate, no power, no required sample size and no empirical conclusion.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 113-115 (PDF pages 121-123): the estimation of the two sides of Bell's inequality from finite series of trials, and the statement that a value is estimated from the results

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Section 5, chapter pages 16-19: the singlet probabilities and the definite-spin ensemble compared through accumulated frequencies of many trials

N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF pages 2-3: the joint probabilities of a Bell experiment estimated from repeated runs, and the assumption that the settings are chosen independently of the specification

items.physical_scope: A conditional finite-sampling analysis for a declared spin correlation arrangement: under a declared independent and identically distributed sampling model with n runs per setting pair, the sample CHSH functional is unbiased, has variance at most 4/n and satisfies the stated Chebyshev concentration inequality; threshold events on either side of 2 have explicitly bounded model probabilities, and every acceptance criterion that rejects a positive-probability outcome sequence fails with positive probability. The item asserts no measured count, no p-value, no power, no error rate, no sample size and no empirical conclusion; the independence and identical distribution of trials is the declared statistical assumption of clause (ii) of P7, not a consequence of the framework.

items.title: Selection and loss: the precise hypothesis under which the CHSH bound transfers to recorded pairs
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Recorded tables are conditional tables.** The arrangement's laws
  $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}$ of
  [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clause (d) describe a declared
  pair of local sign measurements for every setting pair on the declared
  preparation. A comparison with recorded data ordinarily uses only the runs
  in which both stations register an event; the laws of the recorded runs are
  therefore **conditional laws** of a larger model, and they are not the
  arrangement's tables unless a detection and selection model connecting the
  two is declared. This is part of the preparation and apparatus discipline of
  P7 clause (i) ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

- **A sufficient condition for the transfer.** If the full tables admit a
  local-response representation and the recorded runs are exactly those
  specifications lying in a measurable selection event $D$ of the
  specification space with $\mathbb P(D)>0$ — membership is determined by the
  specification alone, using the same event for every setting pair — then the conditional
  tables again admit a local-response representation, with the same response
  laws over the conditional measure, and hence satisfy the CHSH bound
  ([[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]). This is the
  mathematical content of a **setting-independent detection** or
  **fair-sampling** hypothesis for the declared model class. It does not
  require statistical independence of $D$ from the outcomes: reweighting the
  specifications can change the tables.

- **The condition is a hypothesis, not a theorem about detectors.** The
  selection-closure lemma is a conditional statement about the declared model.
  It does not assert that any laboratory detector, coincidence circuit or
  post-selection rule realizes a selection event of the required form;
  identifying a concrete apparatus with such a model is a tested
  identification with uncertainty under P7 and carries its calibration and
  control-experiment qualifications. Efficiency, dead time, misalignment,
  background and drift each require their own declared model.

- **No transfer without a selection model.** If the recorded sample is
  selected by a rule that depends on the settings or on the observed outcomes,
  the selection-closure lemma does not apply, and no claim is made here that
  the CHSH bound constrains the recorded tables. Correspondingly, a deviation
  computed from recorded pairs is a statement about those recorded tables and
  their own declared model; it becomes a statement about the full arrangement
  only through an explicitly justified detection and selection model; the
  condition above is sufficient, not necessary. Finite-sample fluctuations
  are a further, separate matter. The result
  [[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]] assumes $n$ trials per setting pair,
  all $4n$ outcome pairs mutually independent, with each trial law equal to
  the arrangement's table $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}$. It applies to recorded pairs
  only when their declared sampling model satisfies those hypotheses. A
  postselected law different from $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}$, random recorded trial
  counts or correlations induced by selection require a separate analysis;
  the cited result does not supply one. The singlet contrast itself is the
  conditional model computation of
  [[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]].

- **Settings choice.** In a specified experiment model, let $Q_{ij}$ be the
  actual conditional probability law of the specification given that setting
  pair $(i,j)$ is chosen whenever that conditional law is defined. The
  common-law condition required by a local-response representation is that
  these actual conditional laws are all one common law,
  $Q_{00}=Q_{01}=Q_{10}=Q_{11}$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]
  clause (c)); if a setting pair is never chosen, its law must still be
  specified by the comparison model before the four-table representation is
  applied. The possibility that a setting procedure could depend on the
  specification does not establish that the actual conditional laws differ;
  an analysis using a local-response representation must establish their
  equality from its model and the relevant evidence. This page neither
  assumes nor reports such a setting procedure or its conditional laws.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section I.A, PDF page 3: the local decomposition and the assumption that the settings are chosen independently of the specification, the formal basis of a setting-independent selection model

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 113-115 (PDF pages 121-123): the estimation of the two sides of Bell's inequality from recorded series of trials

items.physical_scope: A record of the detection and selection qualification of any comparison between a declared arrangement and recorded coincidences: the recorded tables are conditional tables; the CHSH bound transfers to them when the recorded runs are selected by an event of the specification space that is the same for every setting pair, as the selection-closure lemma states; without a declared selection model no transfer is claimed, and no assertion is made that any real detector satisfies the condition. Finite-sample claims additionally require an explicit sampling model for the recorded law; the cited arrangement-sampling result applies only under its stated independent trial laws. The remark reports no measurement and no efficiency.

items.title: Scope of the examples page: conditional computations, no experiment, and the deferred Bell-test destination
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Three conditional computations in the declared
  framework: the worked comparison at the specified directions between the
  singlet arrangement and the EPR-type product mixture, with both CHSH values
  and an explicit local-response representation of the mixture
  ([[ex-nrqm-bell-worked-angles-and-product-mixture]]); the finite-sample
  behaviour of the sample CHSH functional under a declared independent and
  identically distributed sampling model, with its concentration inequality
  and positive failure probabilities
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]]); and the selection and loss
  qualification, with the precise hypothesis under which the CHSH bound
  transfers to recorded pairs
  ([[rem-nrqm-bell-selection-loss-and-fair-sampling]]).

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment item, no reported count,
  no calibration, no detector efficiency, no loss fraction, no background
  model, no trial-level uncertainty analysis, no p-value and no confidence
  level. The worked tables, the sample functional and the failure
  probabilities are probabilities of the declared models; no number on the
  page is an observation. The identification of any apparatus with the
  declared measurements and of any repetition procedure with the declared
  sampling model is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

- **Deferred Bell-test experiment destination.** The design of the pair
  reserves an experiment item for a Bell test. It is not built here because
  none of the sources read for the pair supplies the required trial-level
  material: a primary or authoritative full report read directly, with the
  source-specific preparation and apparatus, calibration, measured outputs,
  trial count where reported, detection efficiency, losses and
  post-selection, background, the reported statistical treatment and
  systematics, and the source's omissions. The experimental remarks of the
  secondary sources — Binney's reference to the 1972 Freedman-Clauser test
  and its citation of a 1998 photonic test, and the MIT chapter's statement
  that experiments have confirmed violations — motivate the comparison only
  and are not used as measured records; no numerical value from them is
  reproduced. The statistics and primary-report gap named in the design is
  recorded as an open destination.

- **Why a null or shifted sample is not a verdict.** The mixture's tables have
  CHSH value $-\sqrt2$ in absolute value, strictly below both the classical
  bound $2$ and the singlet's $2\sqrt2$
  ([[ex-nrqm-bell-worked-angles-and-product-mixture]]), and the finite-sample
  analysis bounds the probability that a model's sample functional crosses
  either threshold by a strictly positive quantity
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]]). A finite sample therefore does not
  by itself decide between the declared models; a comparison requires the
  full battery of preparation, detection, selection and sampling assumptions,
  and agreement would be evidence about the combined assumptions, not a proof
  of the framework.

- **Model contrast is not an interpretation.** The page compares the tables of
  two declared arrangements and the class of local-response models of those
  tables ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]); it makes no
  claim about the completeness of quantum mechanics, about hidden variables in
  general, about mechanisms or about any interpretation of the violation. The
  boundaries of the comparison are recorded on the pair's first page.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', Section 5, chapter pages 16-20: the singlet probabilities, the definite-spin ensemble and the closing experimental remark without trial-level detail

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1.4, printed pages 111-115 (PDF pages 119-123): the experimental discussion of the Bell comparison and the stated estimation of the two sides from recorded trials

items.physical_scope: A scope record for the examples page of the pair: the conditional computations it contains, the empirical content it does not contain, and the deferred Bell-test experiment destination with its required preparation, apparatus, calibration, loss and statistical qualifications. The record asserts no measured correlation, no count and no empirical conclusion.
